text: LEGACY partial draft of an older planned delivery schema. New educator authoring starts in curation/templates/educator-paths-v1. These tabs are not a complete import bundle and no importer exists. Nothing here reaches a child.

Educators outlining paths should use curation/templates/educator-paths-v1 (see curation/README.md). It is a separate format and is not import-compatible with these tabs; renaming columns is not a migration.

A complete bundle in this older format would also need ASSETS, LESSONS, LESSON_STEPS, LESSON_CHECKS, CHECK_CHOICES and CHECK_HINTS, plus asset bytes, a manifest, compilation, validation and genuine approvals. None exist yet.
Its child phrase, parent observation, strength and date columns are learner records. Do not fill them in a curriculum sheet. Keep real observations in a separate private log outside the repository.

This sheet is a drafting convenience, not a safety boundary. No importer is built yet; a future local importer will decide whether a bundle is valid. Spreadsheet data validation catches typos; it does not enforce anything.

Child name. Account identifier. Exact address, school, phone, email, or location. Raw audio. Raw transcript. Full model prompt or response. Credentials. Medical, behavioral, or diagnostic labels. Family-confidential details.
This is cloud storage. Everything else in Lerni is local by design. A paraphrase is more useful for curation than a quote anyway.
draft -> proposed -> approved. draft/proposed -> rejected. approved -> paused. approved/paused -> retired. Only an educator or parent review moves child-facing content to approved.

For this future bundle format, approval would need a status AND every required attestation in REVIEWS. Filling REVIEWS today changes nothing: the packaged Chain-1 lesson is approved only through review.attestations in its TOML file, following plans/runbooks/chain-1-source-review.md.

interest: parent_approval. source: science. concept/fact/edge: science + child_content. nudge: science + child_content + parent_approval. asset: visual_accessibility + parent_approval. lesson: all four.
No AI, script, or agent writes a REVIEWS row, a TOML attestation, a date, or a hash. The actual reviewer records their own verdict, or the content stays blocked. This is Standing Rule 3.
A parent/prerequisite/related edge states how two concepts relate in the domain. Teaching order is a separate authored sequence. Conflating them corrupts both. This is Standing Rule 4.
Lowercase kebab-case, matching ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$. Stable forever. Row numbers are never identifiers.
ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Real dates only.
Separate with the pipe character. No spaces around it. Order is preserved and meaningful. No duplicates. No item may itself contain a pipe.
Leave genuinely blank. Not N/A, not none, not a dash.
Text must not start with = + @ or -. The importer rejects these outright rather than silently rewriting reviewed content, because a formula prefix is how a spreadsheet becomes an attack surface.
Lowercase true or false.

File -> Download -> Comma-separated values, one tab at a time. Filename must equal the tab name. README, LISTS, EDUCATOR_TODO, and OBSERVATIONS are helper tabs and are never part of a curriculum import.
The Chain-1 lesson is draft with zero attestations. The software refuses to show unreviewed material to a child. See the EDUCATOR_TODO tab for what is outstanding.
